title: 3.6: Species parameterisation for whiteleg_shrimp
text:
← Previous: Parameterise species: asian_seabass
Next: Parameterise species: milkfish →


Overview
This document runs the checking and calibration process on the whiteleg_shrimp model. For a full description of the process, see parameterise_species_seabream.


Species parameters
As we are only running a single representative individual, the Monte-Carlo parameters are not in use.


Load species parameters for whiteleg_shrimp
this_species <- "whiteleg_shrimp"

parameters_species <- read_excel(
  file.path(rawdata_path, 'parameters_species.xlsx'),
  sheet = this_species,
  trim_ws = T,
  n_max = 28
) %>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(used_in_script, value, flexibility)

species_params <- parameters_species %>% pull(value) %>% as.numeric()
names(species_params) <- parameters_species %>% pull(used_in_script)

species_params[["overFmean"]] <- 0.025
species_params[["overFdelta"]] <- 0.0025




Environmental/feed parameters


Load feed and ingredient data and calculate feed composition parameters
feeds_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "feed_profiles_and_composition.xlsx"), sheet = "feed_formulations") %>%
  select(feed, ingredient, proportion) %>% 
  filter(feed == "whiteleg_shrimp-ecuador")

ingredients_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "all_ingredients.xlsx"), sheet = "all_ingredients") %>% 
  select(ingredient, protein, lipid, carb)

digestibility_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "all_ingredients.xlsx"), sheet = "all_ingredients") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(
    protein_digestibility = mean_protein_digestibility, 
    lipid_digestibility = mean_lipid_digestibility, 
    carb_digestibility = mean_carb_digestibility
  ) %>% 
  select(ingredient, protein_digestibility, lipid_digestibility, carb_digestibility)

feed_params <- sum_feeds(
  format_feeds(feeds_df, ingredients_df, digestibility_df)
  )[[1]]




Show feed nutritional profile
tibble(
  Macronutrient = c("Protein", "Lipid", "Carbohydrate"),
  Proportion = c(feed_params[["protein"]]$macro, feed_params[["lipid"]]$macro, feed_params[["carb"]]$macro),
  Digestibility = c(feed_params[["protein"]]$digestibility, feed_params[["lipid"]]$digestibility, feed_params[["carb"]]$digestibility)
) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_percent(columns = c(Proportion, Digestibility), decimals = 1)

The temperature timeseries used is based on the mean current temperatures at farms assigned to this model group in 02_assigning_locations.


Define simulation times and temperature timeseries
# Get current mean temperatures for farms assigned to this model
farm_temps_all <- file.path(prepdata_path, "farm_temps_bymodel", "meanyear_farm_temps_whiteleg_shrimp.qs") %>% 
  qs_read() %>% 
  group_by(model_name, doy) %>% 
  reframe(sst = mean(sst))

farm_temps_all <- rbind(
  farm_temps_all,
  farm_temps_all %>% mutate(doy = doy + 365),
  farm_temps_all %>% mutate(doy = doy + 730)
)

# Get feeding response at each DOY
farm_temps_all$fr <- sapply(
    X = farm_temps_all$sst, 
    FUN = feeding_rate, 
    species_params = species_params
  )
farm_temps_all$fr[is.na(farm_temps_all$fr)] <- 0

# Get a good growing window
grow_days <- species_params[["gd"]] %>% as.integer()
gds <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  mutate(
    roll_fr = slide_dbl(fr, sum, .before = 0, .after = grow_days - 1)
  ) %>%
  slice(1:(nrow(farm_temps_all) - grow_days + 1)) %>%
  slice_max(roll_fr, n = 1) %>%
  mutate(end_doy = doy + grow_days - 1)

times <- c(
  t_start = gds$doy[1],
  t_end   = gds$end_doy[1],
  dt      = 1L
)

farm_temps <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  filter(doy >= times['t_start'] & doy <= times['t_end'])

ggplot(farm_temps, aes(x = doy, y = sst)) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_classic()











Run model with raw parameters


Check that all parameters being passed to the model functions are correct
check_fish_growth_inputs(
  species_params = species_params,
  water_temp     = farm_temps$sst,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = c(
    "t_start" = min(farm_temps$doy),
    "t_end" = max(farm_temps$doy),
    "dt" = 1
  ),
  init_weight    = species_params['meanW'],
  ingmax         = species_params['meanImax']
)


All inputs look good — `fish_growth()` should run without errors.




Run fish_growth() for a representative individual
set.seed(42)
one_fish <- fish_growth(
  species_params = species_params,
  water_temp     = farm_temps$sst,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = c(
    "t_start" = min(farm_temps$doy),
    "t_end" = max(farm_temps$doy),
    "dt" = 1
  ),
  init_weight    = species_params['meanW'],
  ingmax         = species_params['meanImax']
)

cat(sprintf(
  'Initial weight: %.1f g  |  Final weight: %.1f g (%.1f g)  |  FCR (feed/gain): %.2f |  FCE (gain/feed): %.2f \n',
  one_fish[1, 'weight'],
  tail(one_fish[, 'weight'], 1), species_params['CS'],
  sum(one_fish[, 'food_prov'], na.rm = T) / (tail(one_fish[, 'weight'], 1) - one_fish[1, 'weight']),
  (tail(one_fish[, 'weight'], 1) - one_fish[1, 'weight']) / sum(one_fish[, 'food_prov'], na.rm = T)
))


Initial weight: 1.0 g  |  Final weight: 27.5 g (25.0 g)  |  FCR (feed/gain): 0.74 |  FCE (gain/feed): 1.35 










Figure 1: All fish_growth() output variables for a representative individual over a single grow-out period using the default temperature timeseries and feed composition.







Model sensitivity


Set uncertainty of parameters (and remove parameters not being tested for sensitivity)
# "flexibility" refers to the flexibility I'm willing to give each parameter (ie uncertainty)
flex_params <- parameters_species %>% 
  select(param = used_in_script, flexibility) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(flexibility)) %>% 
  arrange(flexibility)




Calculate parameter sensitivity for weight and SGR across plus-minus 10 percent parameter perturbations
species_params_sens <- map(
  flex_params$param,
  function(nm) {
    map(c(0.9, 1.0, 1.1), function(level) {
      species_params[nm] <- species_params[nm] * level
      species_params
    }) %>% 
      setNames(c("low", "med", "high"))
  }
) %>% 
  setNames(flex_params$param)

set.seed(42)
sens_results <- map2_dfr(
  species_params_sens, 
  names(species_params_sens),
  function(sp, nm) {
    map_dfr(sp, function(sp_lev) {
      fish_growth(
        species_params = sp_lev,
        water_temp     = farm_temps$sst,
        feed_params    = feed_params,
        times          = c(
          "t_start" = min(farm_temps$doy),
          "t_end" = max(farm_temps$doy),
          "dt" = 1
        ),
        init_weight    = sp_lev['meanW'],
        ingmax         = sp_lev['meanImax']
      ) %>% 
        as.data.frame() %>% 
        tail(1) %>% 
        select(weight, SGR)
    }) %>% 
      mutate(
        param = nm, 
        level = names(sp)
      )
  }
) 

# Calculate sensitivity
sens_results <- sens_results %>%
  group_by(param) %>%
  summarise(across(c(weight, SGR), ~ (.x[level == "high"] - .x[level == "low"]) / (.x[level == "med"] * 0.2), .names = "{.col}")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = !contains("param"),
    values_to = "sens", names_to = "output",
    names_transform = c(output = as.factor)
  ) %>% 
  left_join(flex_params, by = "param") %>% 
  mutate(param = factor(param, levels = rev(flex_params$param)))


Figure 2 shows how sensitive the model output (individual weight/SGR) is to changes in each parameter - ie the positive/negative impact of increasing that parameter by 10%.


Plot parameter sensitivity as a barplot facetted by output variable
sens_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = param, y = sens, fill = output)) +
  geom_col(colour = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~output) +
  prettyplot()








Figure 2: Sensitivity of final weight and SGR to ±10% perturbations of each model parameter. Values represent the proportional change in output per unit change in parameter.







Hypercube adjustment
The hypercube adjustment uses Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) to search for parameter combinations that bring model output closer to the target weight (commercial size).


Calculate per-parameter sampling ranges from sensitivity and flexibility
# Combine sensitivity across both output variables (mean absolute sensitivity)
sens_combined <- sens_results %>%
  group_by(param, flexibility) %>%
  summarise(mean_abs_sens = mean(abs(sens)), .groups = "drop")

# Range score: inversely proportional to mean absolute sensitivity and flexibility rank.
# Cap 1/sens to avoid blow-up when sensitivity is near zero.
max_inv_sens <- 20
min_inv_sens <- 0.1
sens_combined <- sens_combined %>%
  mutate(
    inv_sens  = pmax(min_inv_sens, pmin(1 / pmax(mean_abs_sens, 1 / max_inv_sens), max_inv_sens)),
    raw_range = inv_sens * (1 / flexibility)
  )

# Cap range changes at +-10%
sens_combined <- sens_combined %>%
  mutate(
    param        = as.character(param),
    sample_range = scales::rescale(raw_range, to = c(0.005, 0.10))
  )




Plot sampling ranges per parameter
sens_combined %>%
  mutate(param = factor(param, levels = param[order(sample_range)])) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = param, y = sample_range * 100)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2171b5", colour = "black", width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Parameter", y = "Sampling range (+-% of baseline)") +
  theme_classic()








Figure 3: LHS sampling range (as a proportion of baseline value) for each parameter. Wider bars indicate parameters that are less sensitive and/or more flexible, giving the sampler more room to explore. Sampling range is capped at +-10% of baseline.







Define target experimental data as a list of experiments - each with its own temperature timeseries and named target outputs
# Each entry in `target_experiments` represents one experimental condition.
# `water_temp` : data.frame with columns `day` (integer) and `temp_C` (numeric)
#                matching that experiment's temperature conditions.
# `targets`    : a named numeric vector of any model output columns to fit.
#                Different experiments can supply different (or overlapping) outputs.

# SS fitness is computed as the MEAN squared error across all (experiment × output)
# observations, so experiments with more targets do not dominate the fit.
target_experiments <- list(
  list(
    water_temp = farm_temps$sst,
    targets    = c(weight_change = unname(species_params["CS"] - species_params["meanW"])),
    meanW      = species_params["meanW"]
  )
)

n_pairs <- length(target_experiments)

# This function processes the fish_growth() output to get it ready for comparison. It's defined here so that if different comparisons are added in this chunk I can change the calculation everywhere at once
get_comparison_stats <- function(df) {
  dfdf <- as.data.frame(df)
  data.frame(
    weight_change = tail(dfdf$weight, 1) - head(dfdf$weight, 1),
    SGR = tail(dfdf$SGR, 1)
  )
}




Generate LHS parameter samples and run model for each (1000 samples x n_pairs with progress updates every 100)
n_samples     <- 2500
param_names   <- sens_combined$param
sample_ranges <- sens_combined$sample_range
n_params      <- length(param_names)

set.seed(42)
lhs_raw <- randomLHS(n_samples, n_params)

# Map [0, 1] to [1 - range, 1 + range] multipliers for each parameter
multiplier_matrix <- sweep(lhs_raw * 2 - 1, 2, sample_ranges, "*") + 1
colnames(multiplier_matrix) <- param_names

# Run model once per experiment for each LHS sample.
# All final-row model output columns are retained so any named target can be used.
lhs_results <- vector("list", n_samples)
start_time  <- proc.time()["elapsed"]

for (i in seq_len(n_samples)) {
  if (i %% 500 == 0) {
    elapsed <- round(proc.time()["elapsed"] - start_time, 1)
    rate    <- i / elapsed
    eta     <- round((n_samples - i) / rate, 1)
    cat(sprintf(
      "Sample %4d / %d | elapsed: %.0fs | ETA: %.0fs\n",
      i, n_samples, elapsed, eta
    ))
  }

  sp <- species_params
  for (j in param_names) {
    sp[j] <- species_params[j] * multiplier_matrix[i, j]
  }

  # Run once per experiment; keep all output columns from the final timestep
  pair_results <- vector("list", n_pairs)
  for (k in seq_len(n_pairs)) {
    wt <- target_experiments[[k]]$water_temp

    change_params <- names(target_experiments[[k]])[names(target_experiments[[k]]) %in% names(species_params)]
    if (length(change_params) > 0) {
      for (c in change_params) {
        sp[c] <- unlist(target_experiments[[k]][c])
      }      
    }

    result <- tryCatch(
      fish_growth(
        species_params = sp,
        water_temp     = wt,
        feed_params    = feed_params,
        times          = c(
          "t_start" = 1,
          "t_end"   = length(wt),
          "dt"      = 1
        ),
        init_weight = sp["meanW"],
        ingmax      = sp["meanImax"]
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(result)) {
      final <- get_comparison_stats(result)
      pair_results[[k]] <- final %>% mutate(sample = i, pair = k, .before = 1)
    }
  }

  pair_df <- bind_rows(pair_results)
  # Only retain samples where all experiments completed successfully
  if (nrow(pair_df) == n_pairs) {
    lhs_results[[i]] <- pair_df
  }
}

Sample 1000 / 2500 | elapsed: 25s | ETA: 38s
Sample 1500 / 2500 | elapsed: 39s | ETA: 26s
Sample 2000 / 2500 | elapsed: 51s | ETA: 13s
Sample 2500 / 2500 | elapsed: 63s | ETA: 0s


Generate LHS parameter samples and run model for each (1000 samples x n_pairs with progress updates every 100)
cat(sprintf(
  "Done. Total time: %.1fs\n",
  proc.time()["elapsed"] - start_time
))


Done. Total time: 63.2s


Generate LHS parameter samples and run model for each (1000 samples x n_pairs with progress updates every 100)
# One row per (sample, experiment)
lhs_results_df <- bind_rows(lhs_results)




Calculate absolute weight difference between modelled and target weight change for each LHS sample
target_wt_change <- target_experiments[[1]]$targets[["weight_change"]]

# Absolute difference between modelled and target weight change per sample
lhs_fit_df <- lhs_results_df %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(abs_diff = abs(weight_change - target_wt_change), .groups = "drop")

# Attach multipliers for inspection of top-performing samples
multipliers_df <- as.data.frame(multiplier_matrix) %>%
  mutate(sample = seq_len(n_samples))

lhs_fit_df <- lhs_fit_df %>%
  left_join(multipliers_df, by = "sample")

# Baseline: run the unadjusted model and compute absolute difference
baseline_result <- fish_growth(
  species_params = species_params,
  water_temp     = target_experiments[[1]]$water_temp,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = c(
    "t_start" = 1,
    "t_end"   = length(target_experiments[[1]]$water_temp),
    "dt"      = 1
  ),
  init_weight = species_params["meanW"],
  ingmax      = species_params["meanImax"]
)

baseline_abs_diff <- abs(get_comparison_stats(baseline_result)$weight_change - target_wt_change)

cat(sprintf(
  "Samples completed: %d / %d\n",
  n_distinct(lhs_fit_df$sample), n_samples
))


Samples completed: 2500 / 2500


Figure 4 shows the distribution of absolute weight differences across all samples.


Plot distribution of absolute weight differences across all LHS samples
lhs_fit_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = abs_diff)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#2171b5", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = baseline_abs_diff, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Absolute weight difference (g)", y = "Count") +
  theme_classic()








Figure 4: Distribution of absolute differences between modelled and target weight change across all LHS samples. Lower values indicate better fit to the target data. The red dashed line shows the baseline (unadjusted) absolute difference.





The parameter multipliers for the best-fitting sample (relative to baseline) are:


Show parameter multipliers for the best-fitting sample
best_sample <- lhs_fit_df %>%
  arrange(abs_diff) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  pull(sample)

best_lhs_results <- lhs_fit_df %>%
  filter(sample == best_sample) %>%
  select(all_of(param_names)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "param", values_to = "multiplier") 
  
# If the change is extremely small (<0.05% of baseline) then the baseline version is kept
best_lhs_results <- best_lhs_results %>%
  mutate(
    multiplier    = case_when(round(multiplier, 2) == 1.00 ~ 1, T ~ multiplier),
    pct_change    = (multiplier - 1) * 100,
    baseline_val  = species_params[param],
    adjusted_val  = baseline_val * multiplier
  ) %>%
  filter(multiplier != 1) %>% 
  arrange(desc(abs(pct_change)))

best_lhs_results %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(multiplier, pct_change), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(baseline_val, adjusted_val), decimals = 4) %>% 
  cols_label(
    param        = "Parameter",
    multiplier   = "Multiplier",
    pct_change   = "% change",
    baseline_val = "Raw value",
    adjusted_val = "Calibrated value"
  )

Calibrated run


Replace calibrated species parameters with new values
new_params <- best_lhs_results$adjusted_val
names(new_params) <- best_lhs_results$param
species_params_new <- species_params
for(nm in names(new_params)) {
  species_params_new[nm] <- new_params[nm]
}
species_params_new["gd"] <- round(species_params_new["gd"], 0)

spn <- data.frame(
  Parameter = names(species_params_new),
  Original_Value = unname(species_params),
  New_Value = unname(species_params_new),
  Pct_Change = 100*unname((species_params-species_params_new)/species_params)
)




Run fish_growth() with the calibrated parameter values
# Run with the default temperature timeseries for the trajectory plot (same as
# the initial checks above), giving a single representative growth trajectory.
set.seed(42)

times <- c(
  "t_start" = gds$doy[1],
  "t_end"   = gds$doy[1] + unname(species_params_new["gd"]) - 1,
  "dt"      = 1
)

farm_temps_new <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  filter(doy >= times['t_start'] & doy <= times['t_end'])

one_fish_new <- fish_growth(
  species_params = species_params_new,
  water_temp     = farm_temps_new$sst,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = times,
  init_weight    = species_params_new['meanW'],
  ingmax         = species_params_new['meanImax']
)

# Also validate against each paired experimental temperature series to confirm
# that the best parameter set improves fit across all observed conditions.
calibrated_pair_results <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_pairs), function(k) {
  wt <- target_experiments[[k]]$water_temp
  sp <- species_params_new
  if (!is.null(target_experiments[[k]]$initW)) {sp["meanW"] <- target_experiments[[k]]$initW}
  set.seed(42)
  result <- fish_growth(
    species_params = sp,
    water_temp     = wt,
    feed_params    = feed_params,
    times          = c(
      "t_start" = 1,
      "t_end"   = length(wt),
      "dt"      = 1
    ),
    init_weight = sp['meanW'],
    ingmax      = sp['meanImax']
  )
  get_comparison_stats(result) %>% mutate(pair = k)
})

# Summary comparison: calibrated vs. target per experiment
# Only columns that appear in each experiment's `targets` vector are shown.
calibrated_summary <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_pairs), function(k) {
  row  <- calibrated_pair_results %>% filter(pair == k)
  tgts <- target_experiments[[k]]$targets
  map_dfr(names(tgts), function(col) {
    data.frame(
      pair      = k,
      output    = col,
      modelled  = row[[col]],
      target    = tgts[[col]],
      diff      = row[[col]] - tgts[[col]]
    )
  })
})

text:
Species parameters
species_params is a named numeric vector containing all bioenergetic, individual-variability, and feeding-rate parameters. The values below are illustrative defaults for Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) — replace with species-appropriate values as needed.


Define species_params — edit this chunk for your species
species_params <- c(
  # --- Bioenergetic parameters ---
  alpha     = 0.04,     # [-]        Feeding catabolism coefficient
  epsprot   = 23600,    # [J/gprot]  Energy content of protein
  epslip    = 36200,    # [J/glip]   Energy content of lipid
  epscarb   = 17200,    # [J/gcarb]  Energy content of carbohydrate
  epsO2     = 13400,    # [J/gO2]    Energy consumed per g of O2 respired
  pk        = 0.05,     # [1/day]    Temperature coefficient for fasting catabolism
  k0        = 0.003,    # [1/°C]     Fasting catabolism at 0 °C
  m         = 0.75,     # [-]        Weight exponent for anabolism
  n         = 1,        # [-]        Weight exponent for catabolism
  betac     = 0.3234,   # [-]        Shape coefficient for the H(Tw) feeding function
  Tma       = 26,       # [°C]       Maximum (lethal) feeding temperature
  Toa       = 16,       # [°C]       Optimal feeding temperature
  Taa       = 2,        # [°C]       Minimum (lower) feeding temperature
  omega     = 0.6542,   # [gO2/g]    Oxygen consumption–weight loss ratio
  a         = 2663,     # [J/g]      Energy density coefficient of somatic tissue
  k         = 0.1715,   # [-]        Weight exponent for energy content of tissue
  eff       = 0.97,     # [-]        Food ingestion efficiency (encounter → ingestion)
  # --- Population / individual-variability parameters ---
  meanW     =  125,     # [g]        Mean initial individual weight at stocking
  deltaW    =  10,      # [g]        SD of initial individual weight
  meanImax  =  0.035,   # [g/g/d]    Mean maximum mass-specific ingestion coefficient
  deltaImax  = 0.0035,  # [g/g/d]    SD of maximum ingestion coefficient
  overFmean  = 0.025,   # [g/g/d]    Mean of overfeeding coefficient
  overFdelta = 0.0045   # [g/g/d]    SD of maximum ingestion coefficient
)

title: 0: A demonstration of the growth model functions
text:
Feed parameters
feed_params is a named list with one entry per macronutrient. Each entry holds three vectors:

proportion: The proportion of each ingredient in the feed (0-1). Note that this will be identical for all macronutrients and MUST SUM TO 1.
macro: The proportion of each ingredient that is composed of that macronutrient (0-1).
digest: The digestibility of that macronutrient, in that ingredient (0-1).

For whole-feed model runs where ingredients are not seperated, proportion == 1 for all list elements.


Define feed_params — edit proportions and digestibilities for your feed
# Example where seperate ingredients within feed are considered
feed_params_ingredient <- list(
  Proteins = list(
    proportion = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.4),
    macro      = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.02),
    digest     = c(0.85, 0.9, 0.75)
  ),
  Lipids = list(
    proportion = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.4),
    macro      = c(0.1, 0.15, 0.9),
    digest     = c(0.2, 0.95, 0.85)
  ),
  Carbohydrates = list(
    proportion = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.4),
    macro      = c(0.6, 0.2, 0.05),
    digest     = c(0.45, 0.5, 0.95)
  )
)

# Example where only whole-feed is considered
feed_params_whole <- list(
  Proteins = list(
    proportion = 1,
    macro      = 0.25,
    digest     = 0.85
  ),
  Lipids = list(
    proportion = 1,
    macro      = 0.2,
    digest     = 0.90
  ),
  Carbohydrates = list(
    proportion = 1,
    macro      = 0.55,
    digest     = 0.65
  )
)

text:
Time vector and water temperature
times controls the integration window and time-step. water_temp is a numeric vector of daily sea surface temperatures for the grow-out period. Here a simple sinusoidal annual cycle is used as a placeholder, as shown in Figure 1.


Define simulation duration and water temperature trajectory
grow_out_days <- 365L   # Duration of the grow-out cycle (days)

times <- c(
  t_start = 1L,              # First time-step index
  t_end   = grow_out_days,   # Last time-step index
  dt      = 1L               # Time-step size (days)
)

# Sinusoidal temperature trajectory: mean 12 °C, amplitude ±4 °C
# Replace with observed or projected SST data for real analyses
set.seed(42)
water_temp <- 12 + 4 * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = grow_out_days)) +
  rnorm(grow_out_days, 0, 0.3)

# Quick check
data.frame(day = 1:grow_out_days, temp_C = water_temp) %>%
  ggplot(aes(day, temp_C)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2171b5") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(species_params["Taa"], species_params["Toa"], species_params["Tma"]),

  annotate("text", x = 5, y = species_params["Toa"] + 0.4, label = "Toa", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = species_params["Tma"] + 0.4, label = "Tma", hjust = 0, size = 3) +

  times     = times

  ggplot(aes(day, n_fish)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#d94701") +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Number of individuals",

Temperature-dependent feeding rate
feeding_rate() returns a scalar in [0, 1] that scales potential ingestion based on current water temperature. The function returns 0 outside the viable range ((T_{aa}) to (T_{ma})) and 1 at the optimum ((T_{oa})).

) %>%
  ggplot(aes(temp_C, feeding_rate)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#238443", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(species_params["Taa"], species_params["Toa"], species_params["Tma"]),

  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05)) +

Running the full farm
farm_growth() is the main wrapper. It runs MC_pop individuals in parallel (Monte Carlo sampling of initial weights and ingestion rates from the distributions defined in species_params), consolidates the individual trajectories to per-time-step means and standard deviations, then scales population-total variables by N_pop.

# Step 1: Get the full (individualised) results for all Monte-Carlo-sampled individual fish in the farm.
farm_results_full <- farm_growth_full(
  species_params    = species_params,
  feed_params       = feed_params_whole,
  water_temp        = water_temp,
  times             = times,
  use_MC_population = TRUE,        # Sample individual variability
  MC_pop            = 200          # Number of Monte Carlo individuals
)

consolidated_results  <- consolidate_farm(farm_results_full)

# Scale certain parameters by farm population to obtain a farm-level version of some of those stats
scaled_farm_results <- scale_farm_population(
  consolidated_results, 
  N_pop = N_pop
)

title: 1: Choosing Species
text:
Coverage of chosen production
There are more model_names than this project can probably reasonably parameterise, so we need a priority list. choosing_ranks_marine gives the priority order in which bioenergetic models might be developed if only marine production is being considered, and choosing_ranks_both gives the priority order in which bioenergetic models might be developed if both marine and brackishwater production is being considered.
We will get different model-development priorities depending on whether the goal is to cover marine production alone or the combined marine + brackishwater total, and they will lead to different outcomes for both environments. Figure 2 shows live-weight coverage when models are added in the order that maximises marine production coverage first, while Figure 3 shows live-weight coverage when models are added in the order that maximises combined marine + brackishwater production coverage.


Calculate per-model production and cumulative coverage for each ranking and scope
# Grand totals for each production scope
grand_total_marine <- FAO_modern_fed %>%
  filter(environment == "Marine") %>%
  summarise(t = sum(drop_units(value), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(t)

grand_total_both <- FAO_modern_fed %>%
  summarise(t = sum(drop_units(value), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(t)

# Total production per model_name, split into marine-only and combined scopes
model_production <- FAO_with_models %>%
  group_by(model_name) %>%
  reframe(
    prod_marine = drop_units(sum(value[environment == "Marine"], na.rm = TRUE)),
    prod_both   = drop_units(sum(value, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# Helper: given a rank table, join production and calculate long-format cumulative coverage
make_coverage <- function(ranks) {
  ranks %>%
    left_join(model_production, by = "model_name") %>%
    arrange(rank) %>%
    mutate(
      cum_marine = 100*cumsum(prod_marine) / grand_total_marine,
      cum_both   = 100*cumsum(prod_both)   / grand_total_both
    ) %>%
    slice_head(n = 20) %>% 
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = c(cum_marine, cum_both),
      names_to  = "scope",
      values_to = "cumulative_pct"
    ) %>%
    mutate(scope = recode(scope,
      "cum_marine" = "Marine only",
      "cum_both"   = "Marine + brackishwater"
    ))
}

coverage_marine_rank <- make_coverage(choosing_ranks_marine)
coverage_both_rank   <- make_coverage(choosing_ranks_both)

# Differences between the rankings
marine_models_unique <- setdiff(unique(coverage_marine_rank$model_name), unique(coverage_both_rank$model_name)) 
both_models_unique <- setdiff(unique(coverage_both_rank$model_name), unique(coverage_marine_rank$model_name))




Plot cumulative coverage under the marine-first ranking
plot_coverage(
  coverage_marine_rank,
  "Coverage under marine-first model ranking",
  marine_models_unique
)








Figure 2: Cumulative production coverage when models are added in the order that maximises marine production coverage (i.e. ranked by marine-only production). Blue line = marine coverage; red line = combined marine + brackishwater coverage. Bold names indicate models that are in the top 20 marine rankings but not the top 20 brackish rankings. Dotted lines show the % of global fed marine production (blue) and marine + brackishwater production (red) that is covered by the first 10 and first 15 models chosen.







Plot cumulative coverage under the combined-environment ranking
plot_coverage(
  coverage_both_rank,
  "Coverage under combined marine + brackishwater model ranking",
  both_models_unique
)








Figure 3: Cumulative production coverage when models are added in the order that maximises combined marine + brackishwater production coverage (i.e. ranked by pooled production). Blue line = marine coverage; red line = combined marine + brackishwater coverage. Bold names indicate models that are in the top 20 marine rankings but not the top 20 brackish rankings. Dotted lines show the % of global fed marine production (blue) and marine + brackishwater production (red) that is covered by the first 10 and first 15 models chosen.

title: 1: Choosing Species
text:
A compromise list
Looking at Figure 2 and Figure 3 above, it makes sense to use the marine + brackishwater as a starting point. However, we can make a minor adjustment: The “general_fish” model will be a parameterisation challenge, given it’s entries are catch-alls for “bony fishes”. Since we don’t have more detailed data than that, it’s probably safest to exclude “general_fish” altogether. Same goes for “general_invertebrate”.
Figure 4 shows the live-weight coverage of a compromised list which excludes “general_fish” and “general_invertebrate”.


Plot cumulative coverage under the compromise ranking
choosing_ranks_compromise <- choosing_ranks_both %>% 
  filter(model_name %in% choosing_ranks_both$model_name[choosing_ranks_both$rank <= 20] | model_name %in% c("asian_seabass", "japanese_amberjack")) %>% 
  filter(!model_name %in% c("general_fish", "general_invertebrate")) %>% 
  arrange(rank) %>% 
  mutate(rank = row_number())

coverage_compromise_rank <- make_coverage(choosing_ranks_compromise)

model_order <- coverage_compromise_rank %>% distinct(rank, model_name) %>% arrange(rank) %>% pull(model_name) %>% rev()

bold_labels <- ifelse(
    model_order %in% all_ready,
    paste0("**", model_order, "**"),
    model_order
  )

vline_15_M <- coverage_compromise_rank %>% filter(rank == max(rank) & scope == "Marine only") %>% pull(cumulative_pct)
vline_15_B <- coverage_compromise_rank %>% filter(rank == max(rank) & scope == "Marine + brackishwater") %>% pull(cumulative_pct)

coverage_compromise_rank %>%
  mutate(model_name = factor(model_name, levels = model_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = model_name, y = cumulative_pct, colour = scope)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = vline_15_M, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#2c7bb6", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = vline_15_B, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d7191c", alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 16, y = vline_15_M, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", vline_15_M),
    hjust = -0.5, vjust = 0, colour = "#2c7bb6", size = 3.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 16, y = vline_15_B, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", vline_15_B),
    hjust = -0.5, vjust = 1, colour = "#d7191c", size = 3.5
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(group = scope), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = bold_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Marine only" = "#2c7bb6", "Marine + brackishwater" = "#d7191c")
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Coverage under compromise model ranking",
    subtitle = paste0("FAO data, (2011– ", max(FAO_aqua$period), ", fed species only)"),
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Cumulative production coverage (%)",
    colour   = "Production scope"
  ) +
  prettyplot() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.y     = element_markdown()
  ) +
  coord_flip()








Figure 4: Cumulative production coverage when models are added in the ‘compromise’ order. Blue line = marine coverage; red line = combined marine + brackishwater coverage. Bold names indicate models that are already parameterised. Dotted lines show the % of global fed marine production (blue) and marine + brackishwater production (red) that is covered by the full 16 models chosen.

title: 1: Choosing Species
text:
Manual curation
A few adjustments can be made to the compromised list to account for these underrepresented countries:

South Korea has a large total production but it is very diverse and poorly represented by the compromise model choice (Table 1). South Korea would be much better represented if flatfish were represented in the chosen models (~33% of production). Including flatfish would also improve the representation of Portugal.
Malta is currently poorly represented, almost entirely because tuna are not in the chosen models (~82% of production).
Mauritius is similarly poorly represented, almost entirely because drums are not in the chosen models (~94% of production). drums and large_yellow_croaker could have similar parameterisation in the model as the groups are closely related, although drums are larger and more specialised than croakers.
~40% of live-weight production in Mozambique is tilapia, and ~33% is meagres (which is actually a kind of drum)
general_fish makes up a large portion of the live-weight production of Bangladesh and Hong Kong (Table 1), but has already been excluded for vagueness. There’s not much we can do about this.

Additionally, while rapa_whelk covers a large amount of live weight production it is only used for a single country: China. It has therefore been excluded. The same logic could be applied to large_yellow_croaker and asian_seabass, both of which also only apply to China. However, asian_seabass has already been parameterised and so can be kept in with less effort, and combining large_yellow_croaker with drums (as they are similar groups) will help increase the relevance of that model.
We have combined most of these adjustments into a new, manually-curated model list. The manual list is based on the compromise list, with the following changes:

olive_flounder has been included to represent flatfishes
tuna and tilapia have been added
rapa_whelk has been removed
red_seabream and gilthead_seabream have been combined into seabream
Croakers and drums have been combined into a new drum_croaker model, which also includes meagres

Figure 7 shows cumulative global production coverage under the new list (ranked by live-weight production)

  filter(
    model_name %in% c(
      "atlantic_salmon", 
      "whiteleg_shrimp", 
      "milkfish",

      "mud_crab", 
      "nile_tilapia", 
      "tiger_prawn", 
      "gilthead_seabream", "red_seabream", 
      "european_seabass",

      "golden_pompano", 
      "grouper", 
      "large_yellow_croaker", "whitemouth_croaker", "meagre", "drum", 
      "japanese_amberjack", 
      "asian_seabass", 
      "tuna",

      )
    ) %>%
  mutate(model_name = case_when(
    model_name %in% c("drum", "large_yellow_croaker", "whitemouth_croaker", "meagre") ~ "drum_croaker", 
    model_name %in% c("red_seabream", "gilthead_seabream") ~ "seabream", 
    TRUE ~ model_name)
    ) %>% 
  group_by(model_name) %>%
  reframe(value = sum(value)) %>%
  arrange(-value) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-value)

Group 1: Simple assignments
In some regions, the number of mapped farms is appropriate for the single model_name that needs to be assigned. These are the easiest to assign and it is done without looking at any temperatures.

title: 2: Assigning farm locations
text:
Group 2: Mapped assignments
In some regions, there are more than enough farms to assign to all the model_names required but some additional decisions need to be made based on farm temperatures. Farm temperatures are extracted from a “mean year” created by data-prep-scripts\historical-sst.R.


Define a function that will extract a meanyear of temperatures from any location
farm_temp_path <- file.path(prepdata_path, "mapped_farms_meanyear")
dir.create(farm_temp_path, recursive = T, showWarnings = F)

global_raster_files <- file.path(prepdata_path, "analysed-SST-MUR25-v4.2_meanyear") %>% 
  list.files(full.names = T) %>% 
  sort()
  
global_raster_stack <- terra::rast(global_raster_files)
names(global_raster_stack) <- paste0("DOY_", 1:length(global_raster_files))

# The actual temperature extraction function extract_point_location_temperature() has been moved to functions.R


This next chunk gets the typical mean year of temperatures for each farm location from a “typical year” constructed from the years 2017 - 2023 (see historical-sst.R for details). The process for each farm is as follows:

Try to extract a temperature vector from the exact farm location point. This was usually successful, however sometimes the temperature vector would come back as all-NA (the data has no temporal gaps but there are some spatial gaps).
In this case, temperature vectors are extracted from the 8 surrounding cells (up to 0.25 degrees away in all directions) and a mean is taken.
If this still returns an all-NA vector, the search is extended to one more cell in the east and west directions only (6 more cells in total, up to 0.5 degrees away). During the extraction process these cells returned a warning, enabling us to see that < 0.5% of cells made it to this step.
If this STILL returns an all-NA vector, the search is extended for a final time to to two more cells in the east and west directions only (12 more cells, up to 1 degree away). Approximately 0.16% of cells made it to this step.
If this STILL returns an all-NA vector, the extraction process finally gives up.



Extract and save the mean daily temperatures at all the farms that might be assigned to Group 2 (or Group 4).
combined <- rbind(farms_required_2, farms_required_4)

for (i in 1:nrow(combined)) {
  cat(sprintf("Starting region %d of %d, extracting %d farms...\n", i, nrow(combined), combined$n_farms[i]))

  this_country <- combined$country[i]
  this_F_CODE <- combined$F_CODE[i]
  this_species_group <- combined$location_group[i]

  aqua_locs_2 <- aqua_locs %>% 
    filter(!farm_ID %in% assigned_farms$farm_ID) %>% 
    filter(country == this_country & F_CODE == this_F_CODE & species_group == this_species_group) %>%
    group_by(farm_ID) %>%
    group_split()

  this_path <- file.path(farm_temp_path, paste(this_country, this_F_CODE, this_species_group, sep = "_"))
  dir.create(this_path, showWarnings = F)

  walk(
    aqua_locs_2,
    extract_point_location_temperature,
    global_raster_stack = global_raster_stack,
    out_path = this_path,
    overwrite = F,
    .progress = T
  )
}

However, there are only a few of them and they’re in countries where there are already plenty of farms (2 in Chile, 1 in Croatia, 1 in Ireland), so these problem farms are simply excluded.

Function to optimise location assignment based on the number of days spent within each model’s ideal ranges
assign_models <- function(ideal_days_df, n_required) {  
  model_cols   <- names(n_required)
  loc_ids      <- ideal_days_df$farm_ID
  n_loc        <- nrow(ideal_days_df)
  n_models     <- length(model_cols)
  n_vars       <- n_loc * n_models
  
  # Extract values matrix internally for indexing convenience
  val_mat <- ideal_days_df %>% select(all_of(model_cols)) %>% as.matrix()
  rownames(val_mat) <- as.character(loc_ids)
  
  obj           <- as.vector(val_mat)
  obj[obj < 30] <- 0
  
  # Constraint 1: each location assigned to at most one model_name
  loc_constraints <- matrix(0, nrow = n_loc, ncol = n_vars)
  for (i in seq_len(n_loc)) {
    idx <- i + (seq_len(n_models) - 1) * n_loc
    loc_constraints[i, idx] <- 1
  }
  
  # Constraint 2: each model_name assigned to exactly n_required locations
  mod_constraints <- matrix(0, nrow = n_models, ncol = n_vars)
  for (j in seq_len(n_models)) {
    idx <- ((j - 1) * n_loc + 1):(j * n_loc)
    mod_constraints[j, idx] <- 1
  }
  
  # Constraint 3: ineligible cells (< 30 days) fixed to 0
  ineligible         <- which(val_mat < 30)
  n_inelig           <- length(ineligible)
  inelig_constraints <- matrix(0, nrow = n_inelig, ncol = n_vars)
  for (k in seq_len(n_inelig)) {
    inelig_constraints[k, ineligible[k]] <- 1
  }
  
  all_constraints <- rbind(loc_constraints, mod_constraints, inelig_constraints)
  all_dirs        <- c(rep("<=", n_loc), rep("=", n_models), rep("=", n_inelig))
  all_rhs         <- c(rep(1, n_loc), n_required[model_cols], rep(0, n_inelig))
  
  result <- lp(
    direction    = "max",
    objective.in = obj,
    const.mat    = all_constraints,
    const.dir    = all_dirs,
    const.rhs    = all_rhs,
    all.bin      = TRUE
  )
  
  if (result$status != 0) stop("No feasible solution found (status ", result$status, ")")
  
  x_mat    <- matrix(result$solution, nrow = n_loc, ncol = n_models, dimnames = list(loc_ids, model_cols))
  assigned <- which(x_mat == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
  
  data.frame(
    farm_ID    = loc_ids[assigned[, 1]],
    model_name = model_cols[assigned[, 2]],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}


“Temperature suitability” here refers only to a species’ feeding response. If a species’ relative feeding response is >0.5 then a temperature is considered suitable for that species. It’s a pretty broad definition of suitability.


Get the ideal temperature ranges for each model
# Default feeding temperature function
feeding_rate <- function(
  temperature,   # current temperature
  Toa,           # optimum feeding temperature
  Tma,           # maximum feeding temperature
  betac = 0.3234 # defualt shape coefficient uses the seabream value from Baldan et al. (2018)
) {
  exp(betac * (temperature - Toa)) * ((Tma - temperature) / (Tma - Toa))^(betac * (Tma - Toa))
}

ideal_temperatures <- unique(FAO_aqua_means$model_name) %>% 
  sort() %>% 
  map_dfr(function(mn) {
    xl <- read_excel(
      file.path(rawdata_path, "parameters_species.xlsx"),
      sheet = mn,
      n_max = 28
      ) %>% 
      clean_names()
    
    fc <- data.frame(temp = seq(-5, 45, 0.25))
    fc$feed_intake <- sapply(
      X = fc$temp, 
      FUN = feeding_rate, 
      Toa = as.numeric(xl$value[xl$used_in_script == "Toa"]),
      Tma = as.numeric(xl$value[xl$used_in_script == "Tma"])
    )

    data.frame(
      model_name = mn,
      min = minna(fc$temp[fc$feed_intake > 0.5]),
      max = maxna(fc$temp[fc$feed_intake > 0.5])
    )
  })




Manual adjustments - some of these assignments are impossible given the species temperature requirements
# All farms in Malaysia are much too warm for abalone
farms_required_2$farm_temps_needed[farms_required_2$country == "Malaysia" & farms_required_2$F_CODE == 71 & farms_required_2$location_group == "Unfed or algae fed bivalve molluscs"] <- FALSE
farms_required_2$cell_temps_needed[farms_required_2$country == "Malaysia" & farms_required_2$F_CODE == 71 & farms_required_2$location_group == "Unfed or algae fed bivalve molluscs"] <- TRUE

# Same with Thailand
farms_required_2$farm_temps_needed[farms_required_2$country == "Thailand" & farms_required_2$F_CODE == 71 & farms_required_2$location_group == "Unfed or algae fed bivalve molluscs"] <- FALSE
farms_required_2$cell_temps_needed[farms_required_2$country == "Thailand" & farms_required_2$F_CODE == 71 & farms_required_2$location_group == "Unfed or algae fed bivalve molluscs"] <- TRUE

# Re-filter after manual adjustments (any rows that moved to group 3 are removed)
farms_required_2 <- farms_required_2 %>% filter(farm_temps_needed & !cell_temps_needed)

# Move the affected rows into group 3 so they get habitat-based extraction
farms_required_3 <- bind_rows(
  farms_required_3,
  farms_required %>%
    filter(
      (country == "Malaysia"  & F_CODE == 71 & location_group == "Unfed or algae fed bivalve molluscs") |
      (country == "Thailand"  & F_CODE == 71 & location_group == "Unfed or algae fed bivalve molluscs")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      farm_temps_needed = FALSE,
      cell_temps_needed = TRUE,
      ISO3_Code = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "iso3c")
    )
)




Assign farms using temperature-based optimisation for mapped regions
for (i in 1:nrow(farms_required_2)) {
  cat(sprintf("Starting region %d of %d...\n", i, nrow(farms_required_2)))

  this_country <- farms_required_2$country[i]
  this_F_CODE <- farms_required_2$F_CODE[i]
  this_location_group <- farms_required_2$location_group[i]

  # Get total number of farms required
  farms_required_2_1 <- farms_required_2 %>%
    filter(country == this_country & F_CODE == this_F_CODE & location_group == this_location_group)

  # Divide farms required between model_names
  FAO_aqua_means_2 <- FAO_aqua_means %>%
    filter(country == this_country & F_CODE == this_F_CODE & location_group == this_location_group) %>%
    mutate(
      region_value = sum(value),
      prop = value / region_value,
      remaining = farms_required_2_1$total_farms_required - n(), # Remaining farms after guaranteeing 1 per row
      raw = 1 + remaining * prop, # Base proportional allocation on top of the minimum of 1
      floor_val = floor(raw),
      remainder = raw - floor_val,
      leftover = farms_required_2_1$total_farms_required - sum(floor_val), # Distribute leftover farms to rows with largest remainders
      rank_rem = rank(-remainder, ties.method = "first"),
      farms_required = as.integer(floor_val + if_else(rank_rem <= leftover, 1L, 0L))
    ) %>%
    select(-prop, -remaining, -raw, -floor_val, -remainder, -leftover, -rank_rem)

  # Put into a named vector for optimisation function
  n_required <- FAO_aqua_means_2$farms_required
  names(n_required) <- FAO_aqua_means_2$model_name

  # Get farm_IDs for the potential farms — exclude any already assigned
  aqua_locs_2 <- aqua_locs %>%
    filter(!farm_ID %in% assigned_farms$farm_ID) %>%
    filter(country == this_country & F_CODE == this_F_CODE & species_group == this_location_group)

  # Get temperature vectors for all the potential farms
  fnames <- farm_temp_path %>% 
    list.files(full.names = T, recursive = T) %>%
    str_subset(paste(fix_int(aqua_locs_2$farm_ID, 8), collapse = "|"))
  fnames_chunks <- split(seq_along(fnames), ceiling(seq_along(fnames) / 100))

  # Check how many days each farm spends within each species' ideal temperature range
  ideal_days <- map_dfr(fnames_chunks, function(idx) {
      df <- map2_dfr(fnames[idx], aqua_locs_2$farm_ID[idx], function(fnm, fID) {
        qd_read(fnm) %>%
          mutate(farm_ID = fID)
        })

      df %>%
        cross_join(ideal_temperatures %>% filter(model_name %in% FAO_aqua_means_2$model_name)) %>%
        summarise(
          ideal_days = sum(sst >= min & sst <= max),
          .by = c(farm_ID, model_name)
        ) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = model_name, values_from = ideal_days)
    },
    .progress = T
  )

  # If there are a huge number of farms, narrow them down by excluding farms that definitely aren't going to be assigned
  means <- rowSums(ideal_days[, 2:ncol(ideal_days)])/(length(2:ncol(ideal_days)))
  means_ints <- tail(order(means), sum(n_required)*3)
  ideal_days <- ideal_days[means_ints, ]

  # Assign farms with the optimisation function
  result <- assign_models(
    ideal_days_df = ideal_days,
    n_required = n_required
  )

  # Add assigned rows to the collector
  result_2 <- aqua_locs_2 %>%
    filter(farm_ID %in% result$farm_ID) %>%
    left_join(result, by = "farm_ID") %>%
    mutate(
      source     = "mapped",
      prod_perfarm = NA
    ) %>%
    select(-c(tonnes_per_farm, NAME_EN))

  assigned_farms <- rbind(assigned_farms, result_2)
}

qs_save(
  assigned_farms,
  file.path(data_path, "intermediates", "assigned_farms_2.qs")
)

title: 2: Assigning farm locations
text:
Group 3: Habitat assignments
This group has no farms available to assign. We will need to create new farms within the correct region and within a reasonable temperature area. Farms should:

Be within 0.5° of the coast (~55 km at the equator)
Be at least 0.25 degrees away from each other (accomplished by resolution)
Have temperatures available from the data
Be within the preferred temperature ranges for their model_names



Load previously-saved EEZ data, restricted to 50km of the coast and divided by FAO region
old_s2 <- sf_use_s2(FALSE)
on.exit(sf_use_s2(old_s2), add = TRUE)  # restore afterwards

land_hires <- ne_countries(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf") %>%
  st_geometry() %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_union()

coastal_buffer <- st_buffer(land_hires, dist = 0.5) %>% 
  st_make_valid()

EEZ_by_FAO_full <- file.path(prepdata_path, "EEZ_data_with_FAO_regions.qs") %>%
  qd_read() %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  st_make_valid() 
  
EEZ_by_FAO <- EEZ_by_FAO_full %>%
  st_intersection(coastal_buffer)




Assign farms based on suitable habitat
assigned_farms <- qs_read(
  file.path(data_path, "intermediates", "assigned_farms_2.qs")
) %>% 
  st_make_valid()

# Accumulate assigned raster cell numbers across iterations so that the same
# cell cannot be selected twice (which would place two farms at identical
# coordinates, violating the >=0.25 degree separation guarantee).
assigned_cells <- integer(0)

for (i in 1:nrow(farms_required_3)) {
  cat(sprintf("Starting region %d of %d...\n", i, nrow(farms_required_3)))
  
  # Information on the current region
  this_country <- farms_required_3$ISO3_Code[i]
  this_country_2 <- farms_required_3$country[i]
  this_fao_reg <- farms_required_3$F_CODE[i]
  this_loc_grp <- farms_required_3$location_group[i]

  # Information on farms needed for region
  farms_required_3_1 <- farms_required_3 %>%
    filter(ISO3_Code == this_country & F_CODE == this_fao_reg & location_group == this_loc_grp)

  # Assign farms needed proportionally to model_names
  FAO_aqua_means_3 <- FAO_aqua_means %>%
    filter(ISO3_Code == this_country & F_CODE == this_fao_reg & location_group == this_loc_grp) %>%
    mutate(
      region_value = sum(value),
      prop = value / region_value,
      remaining = max(n(), farms_required_3_1$total_farms_required) - n(), # Remaining farms after guaranteeing 1 per row
      raw = 1 + remaining * prop, # Base proportional allocation on top of the minimum of 1
      floor_val = floor(raw),
      remainder = raw - floor_val,
      leftover = farms_required_3_1$total_farms_required - sum(floor_val), # Distribute leftover farms to rows with largest remainders
      rank_rem = rank(-remainder, ties.method = "first"),
      farms_required = as.integer(floor_val + if_else(rank_rem <= leftover, 1L, 0L))
    ) %>%
    select(-prop, -remaining, -raw, -floor_val, -remainder, -leftover, -rank_rem)

  # Put into a named vector for optimisation function
  n_required <- FAO_aqua_means_3$farms_required
  names(n_required) <- FAO_aqua_means_3$model_name

  # Filter down to the correct EEZ area
  this_EEZ <- EEZ_by_FAO %>%
    filter(ISO3_Code == this_country & F_CODE == this_fao_reg) %>%
    st_make_valid()

  # land <- ne_countries(scale = "large", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  #   filter(iso_a3 == this_country)
  # ggplot(this_EEZ) + geom_sf(fill = "steelblue") + geom_sf(data = land) + coord_sf()

  # Extract temperatures from cells overlapping this geometry
  temps <- terra::extract(
    global_raster_stack,
    terra::vect(this_EEZ),
    cells = TRUE
  ) %>%
    relocate(cell, .after = ID) %>%
    rename(farm_ID = cell) %>%
    select(-ID) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = contains("DOY"),
      names_to = "DOY", names_prefix = "DOY_", names_transform = as.integer,
      values_to = "sst"
    )

  # Filter out farm_IDs with missing values
  temps <- temps %>%
    group_by(farm_ID) %>%
    filter(!any(is.na(sst))) %>%
    ungroup()

  # Cross with the species preferred temperatures
  ideal_days <- temps %>%
    cross_join(ideal_temperatures %>% filter(model_name %in% FAO_aqua_means_3$model_name)) %>%
    summarise(
      ideal_days = sum(sst >= min & sst <= max),
      .by = c(farm_ID, model_name)
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = model_name, values_from = ideal_days)

  # Remove cells already assigned in a previous iteration (same country/FAO
  # region but different location_group) so no two farms share a cell.
  ideal_days <- ideal_days %>%
    filter(!farm_ID %in% assigned_cells)

  # Assign farms
  result <- assign_models(
    ideal_days_df = ideal_days,
    n_required = n_required
  )
  
  # Record the newly assigned cell numbers so subsequent iterations skip them
  assigned_cells <- c(assigned_cells, result$farm_ID)

  # Re-extract the assigned locations and give them new unique farm_IDs
  locs <- global_raster_stack %>%
    terra::xyFromCell(result$farm_ID) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(global_raster_stack))

  result_3 <- cbind(result, locs) %>%
    mutate(
      farm_ID    = max(assigned_farms$farm_ID, 0L) + row_number(),
      ISO3_Code  = this_country,
      country    = this_country_2,
      species_group = this_loc_grp,
      F_CODE     = this_fao_reg,
      source     = "extracted",
      prod_perfarm = NA
    ) %>% 
    st_as_sf() %>% 
    st_transform(crs = crs(assigned_farms)) %>% 
    st_make_valid()

  assigned_farms <- rbind(assigned_farms, result_3)
}

qs_save(
  assigned_farms,
  file.path(data_path, "intermediates", "assigned_farms_3.qs")
)

    select(-prop, -remaining, -raw, -floor_val, -remainder, -leftover, -rank_rem)

  # Put into a named vector for optimisation function
  n_required <- FAO_aqua_means_4$farms_required
  names(n_required) <- FAO_aqua_means_4$model_name

  # Get farm_IDs for the potential mapped farms — exclude any already assigned
  aqua_locs_4 <- aqua_locs %>%
    filter(!farm_ID %in% assigned_farms$farm_ID) %>%
    filter(ISO3_Code == this_country & F_CODE == this_fao_reg & species_group == this_loc_grp) %>%
    group_by(farm_ID) %>%
    group_split()

  # Get temperatures for mapped farms (already done?)
  fnames <- list.files(farm_temp_path, full.names = T, recursive = T) %>%
    str_subset(paste(fix_int(bind_rows(aqua_locs_4)$farm_ID, 8), collapse = "|"))

  # Check how many days each farm spends within each species' ideal temperature range
  ideal_days_1 <- map2_dfr(fnames, bind_rows(aqua_locs_4)$farm_ID, function(fnm, fID) {
    qd_read(fnm) %>%
      mutate(farm_ID = fID)
    }) %>%
    cross_join(ideal_temperatures %>% filter(model_name %in% FAO_aqua_means_4$model_name)) %>%
    summarise(
      ideal_days = sum(sst >= min & sst <= max),
      .by = c(farm_ID, model_name)
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = model_name, values_from = ideal_days)

  # Get temperatures for potential extracted farm locations
  # Filter down to the correct EEZ area, close to the coast
  this_EEZ <- EEZ_by_FAO %>%
    filter(ISO3_Code == this_country & F_CODE == this_fao_reg) %>%
    st_make_valid()

  # Extract temperatures from cells overlapping this geometry
  temps <- terra::extract(
    global_raster_stack,
    terra::vect(this_EEZ),
    cells = TRUE
  ) %>%
    relocate(cell, .after = ID) %>%
    rename(farm_ID = cell) %>%
    select(-ID) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = contains("DOY"),
      names_to = "DOY", names_prefix = "DOY_", names_transform = as.integer,
      values_to = "sst"
    )

  # Filter out farm_IDs with missing values (data is all or nothing)
  temps <- temps %>%
    group_by(farm_ID) %>%
    filter(!any(is.na(sst))) %>%
    ungroup()

  # Cross with the species preferred temperatures
  ideal_days_2 <- temps %>%
    cross_join(ideal_temperatures %>% filter(model_name %in% FAO_aqua_means_4$model_name)) %>%
    summarise(
      ideal_days = sum(sst >= min & sst <= max),
      .by = c(farm_ID, model_name)
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = model_name, values_from = ideal_days)

  # Combine mapped/extracted farms AND make adjustment - if a mapped farm is suitable, it should be preferred over an extracted farm (artificially boost the ideal days)
  ideal_days <- rbind(ideal_days_1, ideal_days_2)
  ideal_days <- ideal_days %>%
    mutate(across(-farm_ID, ~ if_else(farm_ID %in% ideal_days_1$farm_ID & . > 60, as.integer(. * 1.5), .)))

  # Assign farms - this method is much more likely to generate new farms than assign existing ones
  result <- assign_models(
    ideal_days_df = ideal_days,
    n_required = n_required
  )

  # Separate out mapped vs extracted results
  aqua_locs_4_flat <- bind_rows(aqua_locs_4)
  
  # Extracted: re-derive coordinates from raster cell numbers, assign new unique farm_IDs
  extracted_ids <- result$farm_ID[!result$farm_ID %in% aqua_locs_4_flat$farm_ID]
  locs_extracted <- global_raster_stack %>%
    terra::xyFromCell(extracted_ids) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(global_raster_stack))
  
  locs_1 <- result %>%
    filter(farm_ID %in% extracted_ids) %>%
    cbind(locs_extracted) %>%
    mutate(
      farm_ID      = max(assigned_farms$farm_ID, 0L) + row_number(),
      ISO3_Code    = this_country,
      country      = this_country_2,
      species_group = this_loc_grp,
      F_CODE       = this_fao_reg,
      source       = "extracted",
      prod_perfarm = NA
    ) %>% 
      st_as_sf() %>% 
      st_transform(crs = crs(assigned_farms))

  # Mapped: pull through from aqua_locs
  locs_2 <- aqua_locs_4_flat %>%
    filter(farm_ID %in% result$farm_ID) %>%
    left_join(result, by = "farm_ID") %>%
    mutate(
      source       = "mapped",
      prod_perfarm = NA
    ) %>%
    select(all_of(colnames(locs_1))) %>% 
    st_as_sf() %>% 
    st_transform(crs = crs(assigned_farms))

  assigned_farms <- rbind(assigned_farms, locs_1, locs_2)
}

qs_save(
  assigned_farms,
  file.path(data_path, "intermediates", "assigned_farms_4.qs")
)

text:
← Previous: Assigning locations
Next: Parameterise species: rainbow_trout →


Overview
This document runs the checking and calibration process on the atlantic_salmon model. For a full description of the process, see parameterise_species_seabream.


Species parameters
As we are only running a single representative individual, the Monte-Carlo parameters are not in use.


Load species parameters for atlantic_salmon
this_species <- "atlantic_salmon"

parameters_species <- read_excel(
  file.path(rawdata_path, 'parameters_species.xlsx'),
  sheet = this_species,
  trim_ws = T,
  n_max = 28
) %>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(used_in_script, value, flexibility)

species_params <- parameters_species %>% pull(value) %>% as.numeric()
names(species_params) <- parameters_species %>% pull(used_in_script)

species_params[["overFmean"]] <- 0.025
species_params[["overFdelta"]] <- 0.0025




Environmental/feed parameters


Load feed and ingredient data and calculate feed composition parameters
feeds_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "feed_profiles_and_composition.xlsx"), sheet = "feed_formulations") %>%
  select(feed, ingredient, proportion) %>% 
  filter(feed == "atlantic_salmon-norway")

ingredients_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "all_ingredients.xlsx"), sheet = "all_ingredients") %>% 
  select(ingredient, protein, lipid, carb)

digestibility_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "all_ingredients.xlsx"), sheet = "all_ingredients") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(
    protein_digestibility = mean_protein_digestibility, 
    lipid_digestibility = mean_lipid_digestibility, 
    carb_digestibility = mean_carb_digestibility
  ) %>% 
  select(ingredient, protein_digestibility, lipid_digestibility, carb_digestibility)

feed_params <- sum_feeds(
  format_feeds(feeds_df, ingredients_df, digestibility_df)
  )[[1]]




Show feed nutritional profile
tibble(
  Macronutrient = c("Protein", "Lipid", "Carbohydrate"),
  Proportion = c(feed_params[["protein"]]$macro, feed_params[["lipid"]]$macro, feed_params[["carb"]]$macro),
  Digestibility = c(feed_params[["protein"]]$digestibility, feed_params[["lipid"]]$digestibility, feed_params[["carb"]]$digestibility)
) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_percent(columns = c(Proportion, Digestibility), decimals = 1)

The temperature timeseries used is based on the mean current temperatures at farms assigned to this model group in 02_assigning_locations.


Define simulation times and temperature timeseries
# Get current mean temperatures for farms assigned to this model
farm_temps_all <- file.path(prepdata_path, "farm_temps_bymodel", "meanyear_farm_temps_atlantic_salmon.qs") %>% 
  qs_read() %>% 
  group_by(model_name, doy) %>% 
  reframe(sst = mean(sst))

farm_temps_all <- rbind(
  farm_temps_all,
  farm_temps_all %>% mutate(doy = doy + 365),
  farm_temps_all %>% mutate(doy = doy + 730)
)

# Get feeding response at each DOY
farm_temps_all$fr <- sapply(
    X = farm_temps_all$sst, 
    FUN = feeding_rate, 
    species_params = species_params
  )
farm_temps_all$fr[is.na(farm_temps_all$fr)] <- 0

# Get a good growing window
grow_days <- species_params[["gd"]] %>% as.integer()
gds <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  mutate(
    roll_fr = slide_dbl(fr, sum, .before = 0, .after = grow_days - 1)
  ) %>%
  slice(1:(nrow(farm_temps_all) - grow_days + 1)) %>%
  slice_max(roll_fr, n = 1) %>%
  mutate(end_doy = doy + grow_days - 1)

times <- c(
  t_start = gds$doy[1],
  t_end   = gds$end_doy[1],
  dt      = 1L
)

farm_temps <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  filter(doy >= times['t_start'] & doy <= times['t_end'])

# ggplot(farm_temps, aes(x = doy, y = sst)) +
#   geom_line() +
#   theme_classic()




Run model with raw parameters


Check that all parameters being passed to the model functions are correct
check_fish_growth_inputs(
  species_params = species_params,
  water_temp     = farm_temps$sst,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = c(
    "t_start" = min(farm_temps$doy),
    "t_end" = max(farm_temps$doy),
    "dt" = 1
  ),
  init_weight    = species_params['meanW'],
  ingmax         = species_params['meanImax']
)


All inputs look good — `fish_growth()` should run without errors.




Run fish_growth() for a representative individual
set.seed(42)
one_fish <- fish_growth(
  species_params = species_params,
  water_temp     = farm_temps$sst,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = c(
    "t_start" = min(farm_temps$doy),
    "t_end" = max(farm_temps$doy),
    "dt" = 1
  ),
  init_weight    = species_params['meanW'],
  ingmax         = species_params['meanImax']
)

cat(sprintf(
  'Initial weight: %.1f g  |  Final weight: %.1f g (%.1f g)  |  Approx. FCR: %.2f |  Final SGR: %.1f \n',
  one_fish[1, 'weight'],
  tail(one_fish[, 'weight'], 1), species_params['CS'],
  sum(one_fish[, 'food_prov'], na.rm = T) / (tail(one_fish[, 'weight'], 1) - one_fish[1, 'weight']),
  tail(one_fish[, 'SGR'], 1)
))


Initial weight: 125.0 g  |  Final weight: 3424.2 g (4000.0 g)  |  Approx. FCR: 0.96 |  Final SGR: 0.5 


The model outputs here are looking very reasonable but it looks like harvest weight is being slightly underestimated (Figure 1).








Figure 1: All fish_growth() output variables for a representative individual over a single grow-out period using the default temperature timeseries and feed composition.







Model sensitivity


Set uncertainty of parameters (and remove parameters not being tested for sensitivity)
# "flexibility" refers to the flexibility I'm willing to give each parameter (ie uncertainty)
flex_params <- parameters_species %>% 
  select(param = used_in_script, flexibility) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(flexibility)) %>% 
  arrange(flexibility)




Calculate parameter sensitivity for weight and SGR across plus-minus 10 percent parameter perturbations
species_params_sens <- map(
  flex_params$param,
  function(nm) {
    map(c(0.9, 1.0, 1.1), function(level) {
      species_params[nm] <- species_params[nm] * level
      species_params
    }) %>% 
      setNames(c("low", "med", "high"))
  }
) %>% 
  setNames(flex_params$param)

set.seed(42)
sens_results <- map2_dfr(
  species_params_sens, 
  names(species_params_sens),
  function(sp, nm) {
    map_dfr(sp, function(sp_lev) {
      fish_growth(
        species_params = sp_lev,
        water_temp     = farm_temps$sst,
        feed_params    = feed_params,
        times          = c(
          "t_start" = min(farm_temps$doy),
          "t_end" = max(farm_temps$doy),
          "dt" = 1
        ),
        init_weight    = sp_lev['meanW'],
        ingmax         = sp_lev['meanImax']
      ) %>% 
        as.data.frame() %>% 
        tail(1) %>% 
        select(weight, SGR)
    }) %>% 
      mutate(
        param = nm, 
        level = names(sp)
      )
  }
) 

# Calculate sensitivity
sens_results <- sens_results %>%
  group_by(param) %>%
  summarise(across(c(weight, SGR), ~ (.x[level == "high"] - .x[level == "low"]) / (.x[level == "med"] * 0.2), .names = "{.col}")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = !contains("param"),
    values_to = "sens", names_to = "output",
    names_transform = c(output = as.factor)
  ) %>% 
  left_join(flex_params, by = "param") %>% 
  mutate(param = factor(param, levels = rev(flex_params$param)))


Figure 2 shows how sensitive the model output (individual weight/SGR) is to changes in each parameter - ie the positive/negative impact of increasing that parameter by 10%.


Plot parameter sensitivity as a barplot facetted by output variable
sens_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = param, y = sens, fill = output)) +
  geom_col(colour = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~output) +
  prettyplot()








Figure 2: Sensitivity of final weight and SGR to ±10% perturbations of each model parameter. Values represent the proportional change in output per unit change in parameter.







Hypercube adjustment
The hypercube adjustment uses Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) to search for parameter combinations that bring model output closer to the target weight (commercial size).


Calculate per-parameter sampling ranges from sensitivity and flexibility
# Combine sensitivity across both output variables (mean absolute sensitivity)
sens_combined <- sens_results %>%
  group_by(param, flexibility) %>%
  summarise(mean_abs_sens = mean(abs(sens)), .groups = "drop")

# Range score: inversely proportional to mean absolute sensitivity and flexibility rank.
# Cap 1/sens to avoid blow-up when sensitivity is near zero.
max_inv_sens <- 20
min_inv_sens <- 0.1
sens_combined <- sens_combined %>%
  mutate(
    inv_sens  = pmax(min_inv_sens, pmin(1 / pmax(mean_abs_sens, 1 / max_inv_sens), max_inv_sens)),
    raw_range = inv_sens * (1 / flexibility)
  )

# Cap range changes at +-10%
sens_combined <- sens_combined %>%
  mutate(
    param        = as.character(param),
    sample_range = scales::rescale(raw_range, to = c(0.005, 0.10))
  )




Plot sampling ranges per parameter
sens_combined %>%
  mutate(param = factor(param, levels = param[order(sample_range)])) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = param, y = sample_range * 100)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2171b5", colour = "black", width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Parameter", y = "Sampling range (+-% of baseline)") +
  theme_classic()








Figure 3: LHS sampling range (as a proportion of baseline value) for each parameter. Wider bars indicate parameters that are less sensitive and/or more flexible, giving the sampler more room to explore. Sampling range is capped at +-10% of baseline.







Define target experimental data as a list of experiments - each with its own temperature timeseries and named target outputs
# Each entry in `target_experiments` represents one experimental condition.
# `water_temp` : data.frame with columns `day` (integer) and `temp_C` (numeric)
#                matching that experiment's temperature conditions.
# `targets`    : a named numeric vector of any model output columns to fit.
#                Different experiments can supply different (or overlapping) outputs.

# SS fitness is computed as the MEAN squared error across all (experiment × output)
# observations, so experiments with more targets do not dominate the fit.
target_experiments <- list(
  list(
    water_temp = farm_temps$sst,
    targets    = c(weight_change = unname(species_params["CS"] - species_params["meanW"])),
    meanW      = species_params["meanW"]
  )
)

n_pairs <- length(target_experiments)

# This function processes the fish_growth() output to get it ready for comparison. It's defined here so that if different comparisons are added in this chunk I can change the calculation everywhere at once
get_comparison_stats <- function(df) {
  dfdf <- as.data.frame(df)
  data.frame(
    weight_change = tail(dfdf$weight, 1) - head(dfdf$weight, 1),
    SGR = tail(dfdf$SGR, 1)
  )
}




Generate LHS parameter samples and run model for each (1000 samples x n_pairs with progress updates every 100)
n_samples     <- 2500
param_names   <- sens_combined$param
sample_ranges <- sens_combined$sample_range
n_params      <- length(param_names)

set.seed(42)
lhs_raw <- randomLHS(n_samples, n_params)

# Map [0, 1] to [1 - range, 1 + range] multipliers for each parameter
multiplier_matrix <- sweep(lhs_raw * 2 - 1, 2, sample_ranges, "*") + 1
colnames(multiplier_matrix) <- param_names

# Run model once per experiment for each LHS sample.
# All final-row model output columns are retained so any named target can be used.
lhs_results <- vector("list", n_samples)
start_time  <- proc.time()["elapsed"]

for (i in seq_len(n_samples)) {
  if (i %% 500 == 0) {
    elapsed <- round(proc.time()["elapsed"] - start_time, 1)
    rate    <- i / elapsed
    eta     <- round((n_samples - i) / rate, 1)
    cat(sprintf(
      "Sample %4d / %d | elapsed: %.0fs | ETA: %.0fs\n",
      i, n_samples, elapsed, eta
    ))
  }

  sp <- species_params
  for (j in param_names) {
    sp[j] <- species_params[j] * multiplier_matrix[i, j]
  }

  # Run once per experiment; keep all output columns from the final timestep
  pair_results <- vector("list", n_pairs)
  for (k in seq_len(n_pairs)) {
    wt <- target_experiments[[k]]$water_temp

    change_params <- names(target_experiments[[k]])[names(target_experiments[[k]]) %in% names(species_params)]
    if (length(change_params) > 0) {
      for (c in change_params) {
        sp[c] <- unlist(target_experiments[[k]][c])
      }      
    }

    result <- tryCatch(
      fish_growth(
        species_params = sp,
        water_temp     = wt,
        feed_params    = feed_params,
        times          = c(
          "t_start" = 1,
          "t_end"   = length(wt),
          "dt"      = 1
        ),
        init_weight = sp["meanW"],
        ingmax      = sp["meanImax"]
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(result)) {
      final <- get_comparison_stats(result)
      pair_results[[k]] <- final %>% mutate(sample = i, pair = k, .before = 1)
    }
  }

  pair_df <- bind_rows(pair_results)
  # Only retain samples where all experiments completed successfully
  if (nrow(pair_df) == n_pairs) {
    lhs_results[[i]] <- pair_df
  }
}

Sample 1000 / 2500 | elapsed: 57s | ETA: 85s
Sample 1500 / 2500 | elapsed: 84s | ETA: 56s
Sample 2000 / 2500 | elapsed: 110s | ETA: 27s
Sample 2500 / 2500 | elapsed: 135s | ETA: 0s


Generate LHS parameter samples and run model for each (1000 samples x n_pairs with progress updates every 100)
cat(sprintf(
  "Done. Total time: %.1fs\n",
  proc.time()["elapsed"] - start_time
))


Done. Total time: 135.1s


Generate LHS parameter samples and run model for each (1000 samples x n_pairs with progress updates every 100)
# One row per (sample, experiment)
lhs_results_df <- bind_rows(lhs_results)




Calculate absolute weight difference between modelled and target weight change for each LHS sample
target_wt_change <- target_experiments[[1]]$targets[["weight_change"]]

# Absolute difference between modelled and target weight change per sample
lhs_fit_df <- lhs_results_df %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(abs_diff = abs(weight_change - target_wt_change), .groups = "drop")

# Attach multipliers for inspection of top-performing samples
multipliers_df <- as.data.frame(multiplier_matrix) %>%
  mutate(sample = seq_len(n_samples))

lhs_fit_df <- lhs_fit_df %>%
  left_join(multipliers_df, by = "sample")

# Baseline: run the unadjusted model and compute absolute difference
baseline_result <- fish_growth(
  species_params = species_params,
  water_temp     = target_experiments[[1]]$water_temp,
  feed_params    = feed_params,
  times          = c(
    "t_start" = 1,
    "t_end"   = length(target_experiments[[1]]$water_temp),
    "dt"      = 1
  ),
  init_weight = species_params["meanW"],
  ingmax      = species_params["meanImax"]
)

baseline_abs_diff <- abs(get_comparison_stats(baseline_result)$weight_change - target_wt_change)

cat(sprintf(
  "Samples completed: %d / %d\n",
  n_distinct(lhs_fit_df$sample), n_samples
))


Samples completed: 2500 / 2500


Figure 4 shows the distribution of absolute weight differences across all samples.


Plot distribution of absolute weight differences across all LHS samples
lhs_fit_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = abs_diff)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#2171b5", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = baseline_abs_diff, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Absolute weight difference (g)", y = "Count") +
  theme_classic()








Figure 4: Distribution of absolute differences between modelled and target weight change across all LHS samples. Lower values indicate better fit to the target data. The red dashed line shows the baseline (unadjusted) absolute difference.





The parameter multipliers for the best-fitting sample (relative to baseline) are:


Show parameter multipliers for the best-fitting sample
best_sample <- lhs_fit_df %>%
  arrange(abs_diff) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  pull(sample)

best_lhs_results <- lhs_fit_df %>%

Overview
This document runs the checking and calibration process on the rainbow_trout model. For a full description of the process, see parameterise_species_seabream.


Species parameters


Load species parameters for rainbow_trout
this_species <- "rainbow_trout"

parameters_species <- read_excel(
  file.path(rawdata_path, 'parameters_species.xlsx'),
  sheet = this_species,
  trim_ws = T,
  n_max = 28
) %>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(used_in_script, value, flexibility)

species_params <- parameters_species %>% pull(value) %>% as.numeric()
names(species_params) <- parameters_species %>% pull(used_in_script)

species_params[["overFmean"]] <- 0.025
species_params[["overFdelta"]] <- 0.0025




Environmental/feed parameters


Load feed and ingredient data and calculate feed composition parameters
feeds_df <- read_excel(here("data", "raw_data", "feed_profiles_and_composition.xlsx"), sheet = "feed_formulations") %>%
  select(feed, ingredient, proportion) %>%

The temperature timeseries used is based on the mean current temperatures at farms assigned to this model group in 02_assigning_locations.


Define simulation times and temperature timeseries
# Get current mean temperatures for farms assigned to this model
farm_temps_all <- file.path(prepdata_path, "farm_temps_bymodel", "meanyear_farm_temps_rainbow_trout.qs") %>% 
  qs_read() %>% 
  group_by(model_name, doy) %>%

  farm_temps_all,
  farm_temps_all %>% mutate(doy = doy + 365),
  farm_temps_all %>% mutate(doy = doy + 730)
)

# Get feeding response at each DOY
farm_temps_all$fr <- sapply(
    X = farm_temps_all$sst, 
    FUN = feeding_rate, 
    species_params = species_params
  )
farm_temps_all$fr[is.na(farm_temps_all$fr)] <- 0

# Get a good growing window

gds <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  mutate(
    roll_fr = slide_dbl(fr, sum, .before = 0, .after = grow_days - 1)
  ) %>%
  slice(1:(nrow(farm_temps_all) - grow_days + 1)) %>%
  slice_max(roll_fr, n = 1) %>%
  mutate(end_doy = doy + grow_days - 1)

times <- c(
  t_start = gds$doy[1],
  t_end   = gds$end_doy[1],
  dt      = 1L
)

farm_temps <- farm_temps_all %>% 
  filter(doy >= times['t_start'] & doy <= times['t_end'])

ggplot(farm_temps, aes(x = doy, y = sst)) +
